'''Cephalons''' were a long-lived [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Alien/Legends|alien]] [[Species/Legends|species]] that had [[ganglionic intelligence]], with multiple sub-[[Brain/Legends|brains]] that sent information to a central brain. Cephalons had no visible sensory organs, and to communicate with other beings they had to use [[Computer/Legends|computers]] to translate their thoughts. They also perceived [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] in four dimensions, resulting in an inability to specify [[Time/Legends|past]] or future-tense ideas.

Cephalons were present in the [[galactic community]] by [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]]. At least [[Aoloiloa|one Cephalon]] opposed the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]] as a member of the resistance movement known as [[Whiplash]].

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|It makes no sense. Actually, it's even worse than that. It makes anti-sense.|Den Dhur, on Cephalons' ganglionic intelligence|<ref name="SoS" />}}
Cephalons were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Alien/Legends|alien]] [[Species/Legends|species]] with [[ganglionic intelligence]], meaning that they had a large, sessile, central [[Brain/Legends|brain]] that was connected to multiple semi-autonomous sub-brains. Each of these secondary brains collected information and sent it to the main brain, which was the only intelligence center capable of conceptualization. Cephalons were sessile and globe-shaped, with a random array of tentacles, antennae, and chelae. They had no visible sensory organs common to other species, such as eyes or noses, and they observed their external surroundings by means of [[Electroceptive matrix|electroceptive matrices]]. They lived in large tanks of [[sulfate]] and [[Methane/Legends|methane]], and their mouth consisted of a baleen plate that strained microorganisms from the tank around it.<ref name="SoS" />

Cephalons were a long-lived species.<ref name="Shadow Games" /> A Cephalon's consciousness perceived [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] in a four-dimensional hypermanifold, seeing [[Time/Legends|time]] in the way that most other species saw [[Realspace/Legends|space]]. Their viewpoint allowed them to predict events in the immediate future with great accuracy. Nevertheless, their sense of time prevented them from specifying past or future tenses. To communicate with other beings, their thoughts had to be translated by a [[Computer/Legends|computer]] and projected onto a [[Computer monitor/Legends|monitor]]. However, because of their complex, four-dimensional perception, computers were often unable to effectively translate their thoughts, and the resulting statements were often very confusing to non-Cephalons.<ref name="SoS" />

==History==
{{Quote|Elaboration is/was/will be unnecessary. Sentients are/have been/shall be non-united. Point-pattern at now contingent modalities nonviable. As yet point-pattern in noncollapsed state. Probability matrices undefined. I/we apperceive discontinuity. Suggest cautious/passive/observational mode.|A Cephalon, to Dhur and Tarak|<ref name="SoS" />}}
Cephalons were a part of the [[galactic community]] by [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]]. Due to their inability to speak, they didn't have a name for themselves, and thus were only called Cephalons&mdash;which meant "head" in [[Oldspeak Basic]]&mdash;by the other beings of the galaxy. They were [[Cephalon study|studied]] extensively by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], whose [[Scientist/Legends|scientists]] managed to detect nine distinct emotional states in Cephalons, of which only three remotely resembled those experienced by [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]]. It was also rumored that an Imperial [[Unidentified Inquisitor (Cephalon)|Inquisitor]] had driven himself insane trying to understand the fluctuating states of the Cephalons' four-dimensional mind.<ref name="SoS" />

The Cephalon [[Aoloiloa]] lived on the galactic [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] around 19 BBY. The Cephalon was opposed to the newly-established Empire and joined [[Whiplash]], an underground resistance movement on Coruscant dedicated to helping enemies of the Empire flee the [[Planet/Legends|planet]]. Aoloiloa was visited by two Whiplash members, the [[Gray Paladin]] [[Laranth Tarak]] and ex-[[Journalist/Legends|journalist]] [[Den Dhur]], who hoped to receive the Cephalon's assistance in finding the best route to get their clients offworld. However, due to the Cephalon's complex perception of the galaxy, they were unable to effectively communicate with Aoloiloa.<ref name="SoS" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[Michael Reaves]] created the Cephalons for his [[2008]] novel, ''[[Coruscant Nights II: Street of Shadows]]'', the second installment in the [[Star Wars: Coruscant Nights|''Coruscant Nights'' trilogy]]. The species was later mentioned in the novel ''[[Shadow Games]]'', written by Reaves and [[Maya Kaathryn Bohnhoff]] and released in [[2011]].
